def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) (P : S2 X Y) (T : ℕ),
    ∃ N : S1 X Y, N.D9 ∧ N.d13 = T ∧
      ∀ xs : List X, xs.length ≤ T → N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs

{"translation": "Target defines (names, without asserting or proving) the following proposition:

For all types X and Y, every structure P of type S2 X Y, and every natural number T, there exists a structure N of type S1 X Y (which may depend on X, Y, P, and T) satisfying all three of the following conditions:

1. Acyclicity of the dependency relation (N.D9): There is no element n of N.A1 that has a non-empty directed cycle back to itself under the relation N.D8—that is, no chain n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n of length k >= 1 such that N.D8 c_i c_(i+1) holds at each step. Here N.D8 m n is defined as N.D7 n m, meaning there exist two global states sigma, sigma' : (k : N.A1) -> N.A3 k and an input x : X such that sigma and sigma' agree at every k != m, yet N.a5 n sigma x != N.a5 n sigma' x (so n's updated value can vary when only m's current value is changed). Because Relation.TransGen counts chains of length k >= 1, both self-dependencies (k = 1, where N.D7 n n holds) and longer directed cycles (k >= 2) are forbidden.

2. Exact cardinality (N.d13 = T): The finite type N.A1 has cardinality Fintype.card N.A1 equal to T (exactly T, not merely at most T).

3. Output agreement on inputs of length at most T: For every finite list xs of elements of X such that xs.length <= T (including the empty list []), N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs.

The two structures and their outputs are defined as follows:
- P : S2 X Y consists of two types B1 and B2, initial values b3 : B1 and b4 : B2, transition functions b6 : B1 -> B2 -> X -> B1 and b5 : B1 -> B2 -> X -> B2, and an output function a6 : B2 -> Y. Starting from (b3, b4), P processes xs left to right by simultaneously updating each pair (s1, s2) on input x to (b6 s1 s2 x, b5 s1 s2 x); P.d4 xs applies a6 to the second (B2) component of the resulting pair (so for [], P.d4 [] = a6 b4).
- N : S1 X Y consists of a finite type A1 (equipped with a Fintype instance a2), a family of types A3 : A1 -> Type assigning a state type to each element of A1, an initial global state a4 : (n : A1) -> A3 n, an update function a5 : (n : A1) -> ((m : A1) -> A3 m) -> X -> A3 n, and an output function a6 : ((m : A1) -> A3 m) -> Y. Starting from a4, N processes xs left to right by simultaneously updating a global state sigma on input x to (fun n => a5 n sigma x); N.d4 xs applies a6 to the resulting global state (so for [], N.d4 [] = a6 a4).

What is not required: There are no finiteness, nonemptiness, or size requirements on X, Y, P.B1, P.B2, or the local state types N.A3 n (only the index type N.A1 must be finite, with cardinality equal to T). Agreement between N.d4 xs and P.d4 xs is not required for lists of length greater than T. Finally, dependency in N.D9 is purely semantic (via existence of differing witnesses sigma, sigma', and x; for example, if X is empty, N.D8 is empty and N.D9 holds vacuously)."}

Because Relation.TransGen counts chains of length k >= 1, both self-dependencies (k = 1, where N.D7 n n holds) and longer directed cycles (k >= 2) are forbidden.

- N : S1 X Y consists of a finite type A1 (equipped with a Fintype instance a2), a family of types A3 : A1 -> Type assigning a state type to each element of A1, an initial global state a4 : (n : A1) -> A3 n, an update function a5 : (n : A1) -> ((m : A1) -> A3 m) -> X -> A3 n, and an output function a6 : ((m : A1) -> A3 m) -> Y. divergences.description: The description characterizes S2 as 'a class that includes every system with plasticity', whereas S2 only formalizes discrete-time, deterministic systems with a fixed initial state and time-invariant update functions (excluding continuous-time or stochastic plastic systems).

The description slightly abbreviates the passages when quoting 'plasticity negates the functional equivalence' (omitting 'rapid' and 'between the RNN and the FNN' from [P-O1]) and when stating that equivalence breaks for all t > t0 'under plasticity' (omitting 'any nontrivial' from [P-O3]), though the substantive sense is preserved.

judgement.summary: The Lean statement accurately matches the author's description in its quantifiers, exact unit count, acyclicity condition, and finite-horizon history-by-history equivalence, and the description fairly reports what the passages claim and concede while transparently noting the differences in formalism. Only minor caveats apply regarding the discrete-time deterministic idealization in S2 and slight abbreviations of qualifiers from the passages.
